chapter_summary: Proverbs 13 continues Solomon's collection of sharp, contrasting wisdom sayings. The chapter holds together a consistent theme: how we speak, work, and respond to correction shapes our whole life. The wise person listens — to parents, to God's word, and to godly correction. The diligent person is rewarded; the lazy person ends up with nothing. Those who choose righteousness walk in the light; those who choose wickedness stumble toward ruin. Children who are truly loved are corrected and shaped toward wisdom. The chapter ends with a powerful image: the righteous person eats to satisfaction, but the wicked go hungry — even in the things that matter most.
main_lesson: Listening to wise teaching and working hard with honesty leads to a good life. Those who ignore God's words and choose their own way will face trouble.

memory_verse.kjv: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
memory_verse.little_bible: Walk with wise people and you will grow wise. But choose foolish friends and it will hurt you.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 13 is rich territory for family discipleship because it touches the most practical corners of a child's life: how they receive correction, how they work, who they choose as friends, and how they speak. Verse 1 sets the tone immediately — wisdom begins with listening to your father's instruction. This is not just social obedience; it is the posture of a teachable heart toward God Himself. Use this as an opportunity to talk about why parents correct children — not out of harshness but out of love, as verse 24 makes explicit.

Verses 4 and 11 together offer a powerful economic discipleship lesson: laziness produces poverty, but patient diligent labour grows into increase. In a world of instant gratification, this is counter-cultural wisdom. Help children see that what is built slowly and honestly is stronger than what is gained quickly and carelessly.

Verse 12 is one of the most emotionally resonant verses in all of Proverbs — 'hope deferred makes the heart sick.' Children understand this feeling. Use it to talk about how God does not always answer immediately, but His promises are always worth waiting for. Verse 20 on friendship is perhaps the most immediately applicable to children in middle childhood. Who we walk with shapes who we become. This is not about avoiding people — it is about the formative power of close friendship. Help your children think carefully and prayerfully about their friendships.
application_for_children: This week, practise being a good listener — at home, in school, and when you read the Bible. When a parent or teacher corrects you, say thank you instead of arguing. Ask God to help you choose wise friends.

verses.kjv: A wise son heareth his father's instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.
verses.little_bible: A wise child listens to their father's teaching. A proud child refuses to hear any correction.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A wise child listens to their father.
verses.meaning: Wisdom begins with receptivity — a teachable heart that welcomes a parent's instruction. The 'scorner' is not merely rebellious; they are proud enough to reject even needed correction. This verse frames the whole chapter: those who listen grow wise; those who refuse to hear bring ruin on themselves.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen to my parents today.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it hard to listen when someone corrects you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a home atmosphere where receiving correction feels safe and loving, rather than shameful or punitive? How does the way we correct shape whether our children become scorners or listeners?
verses.do_it_today: When a parent or teacher teaches you something today, stop what you are doing and really listen. Do not argue.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting attentively at the feet of a kind father who is teaching, warm golden light around them, versus another child walking away with arms crossed, refusing to listen, gentle watercolour style

verses.kjv: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth: but the soul of the transgressors shall eat violence.
verses.little_bible: Good words bring good results — like eating good fruit. But those who do wrong will taste the harm their own choices produce.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good words bring good things back to you.
verses.meaning: Speech produces consequences — both positive and negative. The 'fruit of the mouth' means that our words, over time, yield a harvest that comes back to us. Righteous speech produces blessing; the words and deeds of transgressors yield a harvest of violence and harm. We will eventually eat what we sow.
verses.prayer: God, help my words bring good things.
verses.discussion_question: Have your good words ever brought something good back?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that their words are seeds — and that what they say plants something that will one day come back to them as a harvest?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to say three good, kind, honest things today. Think of them as seeds you are planting.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking kind words that grow into a fruit tree beside them, bright fruit hanging low, versus another figure whose harsh words grow into thorns, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.
verses.little_bible: Guard your mouth and you guard your life. Talk carelessly and it will bring you to ruin.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Guard your mouth and guard your life.
verses.meaning: There is a direct link between speech and life-outcomes. Careless, unguarded talk creates exposure to enemies, conflict, and destruction. Keeping the mouth — disciplining what we say — is a life-protecting practice. The 'opening wide' of the lips pictures reckless, unfiltered speech that cannot be taken back.
verses.prayer: God, guard my mouth and my life.
verses.discussion_question: Has something you said ever caused big trouble? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children develop the habit of pausing before speaking — of 'keeping' the mouth — so that words are intentional rather than reactive?
verses.do_it_today: Before you say anything in a difficult moment today, count to three and ask: 'Should I say this?' Then decide.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child gently holding their hand over their mouth in a moment of wise restraint, a safe glowing path before them, contrasted with another child speaking carelessly with words flying wildly outward, watercolour style

verses.kjv: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
verses.little_bible: The lazy person wants many things but ends up with nothing. The hard worker gets more and more.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hard workers get what they need. Lazy people stay empty.
verses.meaning: Desire without action produces nothing. The sluggard's wants are real, but wanting without working cannot produce results. The diligent person, by contrast, sees their soul 'made fat' — a Hebrew picture of abundance, satisfaction, and flourishing. Diligence turns desire into reality.
verses.prayer: God, help me work hard and not be lazy.
verses.discussion_question: What is something you want but have not worked toward yet?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate diligence rather than just desire in our children — teaching them to move from wanting to working, and from dreaming to doing?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one thing you have wanted to do but have not started. Take one real step toward it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two children side by side: one sitting and wishing with an empty bowl, the other working in a garden with an overflowing basket of produce, warm watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: A righteous man hateth lying: but a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.
verses.little_bible: A righteous person hates lying. But a wicked person does shameful things and ends up disgraced.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteous people hate lies. Lying brings shame.
verses.meaning: Hatred of lying is a mark of true righteousness — not just avoiding lies when convenient, but genuinely hating them as God does. The wicked person, by contrast, becomes repulsive through their dishonesty and ultimately comes to public shame. Character and reputation are inseparable.
verses.prayer: God, give me a heart that hates lying.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God want us to hate lying?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate not just rule-following honesty but a genuine love of truth — so that our children hate lying the way God hates it?
verses.do_it_today: If there is anything you have not been fully honest about, make it right today with one small, true word.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child recoiling from a shadowy figure representing a lie, their face showing honest distaste, the righteous child standing in clear bright light, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Righteousness keepeth him that is upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
verses.little_bible: Righteousness keeps the upright person safe on the right path. But doing wrong trips up the sinner and brings them down.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteousness keeps you safe on the right path.
verses.meaning: Righteousness is not merely a moral quality — it is a protecting force. It guards those who walk in it, keeping them from stumbling. Wickedness, by contrast, has a self-defeating quality: it overthrows, trips up, and brings down the very person who practices it. Sin carries its own judgment.
verses.prayer: God, let righteousness keep me on Your path.
verses.discussion_question: How does doing right protect you from getting into trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that righteousness is not restrictive but protective — that God's ways are a guard, not a cage?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one right choice that kept you out of trouble. Thank God for how righteousness protected you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking safely along a bright steady path, a gentle protective glow around them from their righteousness, while a shadowy figure trips and falls off a crooked road, watercolour style

verses.kjv: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: and there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches.
verses.little_bible: Some people look rich but have nothing that matters. Some look poor but are rich in what truly counts.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Real riches are not always what you can see.
verses.meaning: This verse punctures appearances. True wealth is not what we display. Some who appear wealthy are inwardly bankrupt — no real relationships, no integrity, no peace with God. Some who appear poor are genuinely rich — in wisdom, love, godliness, and contentment. Proverbs consistently subverts the world's definition of success.
verses.prayer: God, make me rich in what truly matters.
verses.discussion_question: What are some riches that money cannot buy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a theology of true wealth — one that values godliness, love, and character above financial wealth or social appearance?
verses.do_it_today: Name three ways your family is rich that have nothing to do with money. Thank God for each one.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two contrasting figures: a richly dressed child who looks empty and sad, and a simply dressed child who is laughing and surrounded by love and light, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: The ransom of a man's life are his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.
verses.little_bible: Wealth can get a rich person out of some trouble. But a poor person does not have that worry — and sometimes that is freeing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wealth can be a target. The poor have peace from that danger.
verses.meaning: Wealth creates vulnerability — it makes a person a target for extortion, threats, or demands. The poor person, ironically, hears no such rebuke or ransom demand, because there is nothing worth taking. Riches bring not only comfort but a particular kind of danger. True security is not in wealth but in God.
verses.prayer: God, let You — not wealth — be my security.
verses.discussion_question: Can being very rich bring problems? What kinds?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children find their security in God rather than in wealth — and understand that material riches bring both opportunity and vulnerability?
verses.do_it_today: Think: what do you trust most for safety? Write it down. Is God on that list?
verses.illustration_prompt: A wealthy figure looking nervously over their shoulder, weighed down by their treasure, compared to a simple poor child walking freely in sunlight, gentle watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The light of the righteous rejoiceth: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person's light shines bright and rejoices! But the wicked person's light will one day go out forever.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous shine. The wicked go dark.
verses.meaning: Light and lamp are images of life, vitality, and hope. The righteous person's light rejoices — it is alive, burning brightly, full of energy. The wicked person's lamp, though perhaps burning for a season, will ultimately be extinguished. The contrast is between a joyful, enduring light and one that will eventually go dark.
verses.prayer: God, let Your light shine through my life.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean for someone's life to shine like a light?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model and cultivate a life that shines — full of righteous joy rather than the flickering false brightness of wickedness?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that lets your light shine — a kind act, an honest word, a deed that brings God glory.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright joyful lamp glowing warmly on the left representing the righteous, and a spluttering dim lamp going out on the right representing the wicked, soft and meaningful watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.
verses.little_bible: Pride is the root of every argument and fight. But those who take good advice grow in wisdom.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride starts fights. Good advice brings wisdom.
verses.meaning: The word 'only' is striking — pride is the exclusive root of contention. Arguments, conflicts, and strife are ultimately pride problems: someone insisting on being right, refusing to yield, or unwilling to submit. The remedy is the opposite of pride: being 'well-advised' — willing to listen, seek counsel, and receive wisdom from others.
verses.prayer: God, keep pride out of my heart.
verses.discussion_question: Has pride ever started a fight or argument? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: How do we identify pride in ourselves and our children — and teach the humble practice of seeking and receiving good counsel?
verses.do_it_today: In one situation today, choose to listen to advice instead of insisting you are right. See what happens.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two children arguing, a dark shadow of pride above them, contrasted with a child sitting quietly and listening to a wise adviser, warm peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.
verses.little_bible: Money gained quickly through foolish means will shrink away. But what you build slowly through hard work will grow and grow.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Slow honest work grows. Quick easy money shrinks.
verses.meaning: Wealth obtained without real work — through tricks, shortcuts, gambling, or dishonesty — has no staying power. But patient, diligent labour produces lasting increase. This is a consistent thread in Proverbs: character and process matter as much as outcome. What is built on right foundations lasts.
verses.prayer: God, help me build slowly and honestly.
verses.discussion_question: Why does hard work feel better than easy shortcuts?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand and appreciate the value of gradual, honest, patient increase — in an age of instant results and quick money?
verses.do_it_today: Work on something today that takes patience. A chore, a skill, a homework task. Do it slowly and well.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two contrasting money bags: one shiny and flashy but with holes leaking coins away, the other plain but solid and growing bigger through steady labour, gentle watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
verses.little_bible: Waiting too long for something you hope for makes your heart ache. But when it finally comes, it feels like a whole tree of life blooming!
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Waiting makes the heart hurt. But answered hope brings joy.
verses.meaning: This is one of the most emotionally honest verses in Scripture. Hope deferred — delayed, unfulfilled, seemingly forgotten — produces a very real sickness of the heart. God does not dismiss this feeling. But when the desire finally comes, the relief and joy are overwhelming — like a tree of life, abundant and full of what sustains. Waiting is hard; God knows it. But His timing produces life.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You while I wait.
verses.discussion_question: What is something you are waiting for? How does waiting make you feel?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children hold on through seasons of hope-deferral — trusting that God's timing is not forgetfulness, and that what He grants is worth the wait?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one hope you are waiting on. Give it to God in prayer. Then wait in trust, not in worry.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child waiting alone with a weary face, hope flickering like a small candle — then the next scene: the same child with arms wide open as a great tree of life blooms around them, joyful watercolour panels

verses.kjv: Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.
verses.little_bible: Anyone who despises God's word will be destroyed. But the one who honours and fears God's commands will be rewarded.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honour God's word and be rewarded.
verses.meaning: Contempt for God's word is not a neutral attitude — it leads directly to destruction. The stakes of how we relate to Scripture could not be higher. By contrast, reverencing God's commandments — taking them seriously, obeying them from a heart of holy respect — results in reward. Our posture toward the Word of God determines our outcome.
verses.prayer: God, help me honour and obey Your word.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to despise or ignore God's word?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a household culture of deep reverence for Scripture — not fearful but genuinely honouring, treating the Bible as the living Word of God?
verses.do_it_today: Read one verse of the Bible today. Before you read it, say: 'God, I respect and want to obey Your word.' Then read and obey.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child reverently holding an open Bible with a warm glow rising from the pages, contrasted with a figure carelessly tossing a book aside in darkness, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
verses.little_bible: The teaching of the wise is like a fountain of life. It helps you escape every deadly trap.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise teaching is a fountain that gives life.
verses.meaning: The wise person's instruction is life-giving and liberating — like a flowing fountain in a desert. Critically, it keeps people away from the 'snares of death' — the hidden traps and deadly pitfalls that surround them. Wisdom does not just give life positively; it actively protects from what destroys life. This connects with the repeated theme in Proverbs of wisdom as the path that avoids destruction.
verses.prayer: God, let wise teaching guide and protect me.
verses.discussion_question: How has wise teaching kept you out of trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we impart wisdom to our children not as rules to obey but as a life-giving fountain — instruction that frees rather than merely restricts?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one piece of wise teaching you have received. How has it protected you? Thank the person who taught you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A clear fountain of life-giving water flowing in a sunny landscape, a child drinking from it joyfully, deadly traps and thorns avoided all around, bright watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Good understanding giveth favour: but the way of transgressors is hard.
verses.little_bible: Good understanding wins you favour with people. But the path of those who do wrong is rough and hard.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good understanding wins favour with others.
verses.meaning: Understanding here implies not just intelligence but discernment — knowing how to act rightly in every situation. Such a person naturally gains favour from others and from God. The transgressors' way, by contrast, is described as 'hard' — literally unyielding, enduring, harsh. The path of sin is not easy — it is grinding and relentless. This is the opposite of the world's promise that wrongdoing is the easy road.
verses.prayer: God, give me good understanding today.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of someone with good understanding?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop real understanding — wisdom that shows up in how they treat people, make decisions, and read situations rightly?
verses.do_it_today: Before reacting to a hard situation today, stop and ask: 'What is the wise and understanding response here?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a thoughtful, understanding expression receiving warm smiles from those around them, a wide clear path before them, versus a figure struggling on a rough rocky road, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Every prudent man dealeth with knowledge: but a fool layeth open his folly.
verses.little_bible: A wise and careful person acts with knowledge. But a foolish person shows off their foolishness for everyone to see.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Careful people act with knowledge. Fools show their foolishness.
verses.meaning: Prudence — careful, thoughtful action — deals in knowledge. The prudent person does not act impulsively but from what they actually know. The fool, by contrast, 'lays open' their folly — their foolishness is spread out and displayed, like merchandise in a market, for everyone to observe. Wisdom works quietly; folly advertises itself.
verses.prayer: God, help me act carefully with knowledge.
verses.discussion_question: How do wise actions look different from foolish ones?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate prudence — thoughtful, knowledge-based action — in our children, rather than impulsive or show-off behaviour?
verses.do_it_today: Before making one decision today, stop and ask: 'What do I actually know about this? What is the careful, wise choice?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child carefully examining a situation thoughtfully before acting, knowledge like a gentle light in their hands, compared to a foolish child acting wildly with their folly visible to all, watercolour style

verses.kjv: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador is health.
verses.little_bible: A messenger who cannot be trusted causes trouble everywhere. But a faithful ambassador brings healing and peace.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A faithful messenger brings health and peace.
verses.meaning: The reliability of a messenger is critical — in the ancient world and in every age. A wicked or untrustworthy messenger corrupts the communication between people; they bring mischief in the very act of conveying a message. A faithful ambassador, by contrast, is described as 'health' — they heal relationships, accurately convey truth, and serve those who trust them. This applies to every person who carries news, advice, or God's message.
verses.prayer: God, help me be faithful and trustworthy.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when someone shares a message incorrectly or dishonestly?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that every message they carry — between friends, in the family, in prayer — has real consequences, and faithfulness matters?
verses.do_it_today: Be accurate today in everything you repeat or report. Do not add to it, take from it, or twist it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A trustworthy child carrying a glowing message carefully between two smiling people, the message bringing health and peace, compared to a careless messenger scattering twisted words, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.
verses.little_bible: The person who refuses teaching ends up poor and ashamed. But the one who welcomes correction will be honoured.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Welcome correction and be honoured.
verses.meaning: Refusing instruction is not a neutral choice — it leads to poverty and shame, two outcomes that strip a person of dignity and provision. But receiving reproof — genuinely regarding it, taking it seriously — produces honour. The person who can be taught is the person who can grow. This verse is a powerful argument for humility in the face of correction.
verses.prayer: God, help me welcome correction and grow.
verses.discussion_question: Has a correction ever helped you get better?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children move from defensive reactions to correction toward grateful reception — seeing correction as a gift that leads to honour?
verses.do_it_today: The next time someone corrects you today, say: 'Thank you.' Mean it. Then act on what they said.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child bowing their head humbly to receive correction from a kind teacher, a crown of honour beginning to form above their head, watercolour warm and affirming scene

verses.kjv: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul: but it is abomination to fools to depart from evil.
verses.little_bible: Reaching a good goal is sweet to the soul. But fools hate the idea of leaving their wrong ways behind.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good goals reached are sweet. Fools refuse to leave evil.
verses.meaning: The first half celebrates the sweetness of accomplishment — when a righteous desire is fulfilled, the soul experiences deep satisfaction. But the second half is stark: fools find it an abomination to leave evil. They are so attached to their wrongdoing that abandoning it feels revolting to them. This reveals the hardening power of sin: it eventually makes repentance feel undesirable.
verses.prayer: God, help me turn from wrong without delay.
verses.discussion_question: Why would someone not want to stop doing something wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that the longer we stay in wrong patterns, the harder it becomes to leave them — and therefore why early repentance and obedience matters?
verses.do_it_today: Is there a wrong habit in your life? Decide to take one step away from it today. Do not wait.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child joyfully celebrating reaching a good goal, sweetness and light all around, contrasted with a figure stubbornly clutching darkness and refusing to let go, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
verses.little_bible: Walk with wise people and you will grow wise. Choose foolish companions and you will be destroyed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Walk with wise people and grow wise.
verses.meaning: Friendship is formative. This is one of the most practically urgent verses in Proverbs for children and adults alike. Those we spend time with shape our thinking, values, habits, and ultimately our destiny. Walking with the wise produces wisdom — through exposure, imitation, conversation, and accountability. But close companionship with fools leads to destruction, not because foolishness is inevitable but because it is contagious and formative. Choose friends wisely.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose wise friends.
verses.discussion_question: How do your friends change the way you think or act?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children make prayerful and intentional friendship choices — understanding the formative power of close companions without becoming isolated or unkind to others?
verses.do_it_today: Think about who you spend the most time with. Do they help you grow wiser? Pray about your friendships today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking joyfully alongside wise, kind companions on a bright path, all of them growing together, contrasted with a child being pulled down a dark road by foolish companions, warm watercolour

verses.kjv: Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.
verses.little_bible: Evil chases after those who do wrong and catches up with them. But good things come back to the righteous.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Evil chases sinners. Good comes back to the righteous.
verses.meaning: There is a moral order to the universe that God has built in. Evil does not merely threaten sinners from a distance — it actively pursues them, tracking them down. By contrast, good is 'repaid' to the righteous — it returns to them, as a merchant repays what is owed. God's justice and goodness operate as real forces in the world, not just concepts.
verses.prayer: God, let me choose right and trust You.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time when a wrong choice kept causing more problems?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand God's moral order — that choices have consequences that follow us — without being simplistic about suffering or prosperity?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one right thing today and trust God to repay it with good. Then wait and watch.
verses.illustration_prompt: A dark shadow of consequences pursuing a figure who is running away from their wrong choices, compared to a righteous child standing still as good things flow toward them, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.
verses.little_bible: A good person builds a legacy for their grandchildren. Even what the sinner stores up will end up with the righteous.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people build a lasting legacy for their family.
verses.meaning: Generational thinking is built into wisdom. The good person does not just live for themselves or even just for their children — they think of their grandchildren. Legacy is a key concept here: character, wisdom, and godly wealth outlast a single life. The second half reinforces God's sovereign control: even what wicked people accumulate is ultimately transferred to the just — a recurring biblical theme of reversal.
verses.prayer: God, help me build a good legacy.
verses.discussion_question: What would you want your grandchildren to remember about how you lived?
verses.family_discussion: What inheritance — spiritual, relational, and material — are we building for our grandchildren and beyond? How does today's faithfulness shape that legacy?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a grandparent or older person what they hope to leave behind for their family. Listen carefully.
verses.illustration_prompt: A grandparent and grandchild together in a warm garden, the grandfather passing something precious and glowing from their hands to the child's hands, generational love, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Much food is in the tillage of the poor: but there is that is destroyed for want of judgment.
verses.little_bible: A poor person's field can produce much food with wise tending. But some lose everything because they lack good judgment.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise judgment makes even small things fruitful.
verses.meaning: The land of the poor, when properly tended with wisdom, can yield abundant food. This is encouraging: circumstances do not determine outcome as much as wisdom and good judgment do. But poor judgment can destroy even potential abundance. Resources — large or small — require wisdom to bear fruit. Judgment (discernment, wise decision-making) is a form of stewardship.
verses.prayer: God, give me good judgment in all things.
verses.discussion_question: Can a small thing grow big if you take care of it wisely?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop good judgment and stewardship — understanding that what they have is enough when managed with wisdom?
verses.do_it_today: Choose something small you are responsible for and tend it carefully and wisely today. Do not neglect it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A simple small garden plot being carefully tended by a child in modest clothes, the soil producing abundant vegetables and fruit through careful wise effort, watercolour garden scene

verses.kjv: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
verses.little_bible: A parent who never corrects their child does not truly love them. But a parent who lovingly disciplines early shows real love.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A loving parent corrects their child early.
verses.meaning: This verse is often misunderstood. It is not a call to harshness but a call to love that is willing to correct. 'Sparing the rod' means refusing to discipline — and the verse identifies this as a form of hatred, not gentleness. The parent who truly loves a child is the one who disciplines them promptly ('betimes' — early, in good time), shaping them before wrong patterns harden. True love does the hard work of correction.
verses.prayer: God, help me receive correction as love.
verses.discussion_question: Has a parent ever corrected you because they loved you? How did you know it was love?
verses.family_discussion: How do we make our correction feel like love to our children — so they do not experience discipline as rejection but as investment? How do we correct early, consistently, and warmly?
verses.do_it_today: If a parent corrected you recently, think about why they did it. Say thank you to them for loving you enough to correct you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A kind, gentle parent kneeling down to correct a child with a warm but serious expression, the child's face showing understanding and trust — love made visible in discipline, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person is truly satisfied — their soul is fed and full. But the wicked person's belly is always wanting, never full.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous are satisfied. The wicked are always hungry.
verses.meaning: The chapter closes with an image of satisfaction versus craving. The righteous person eats 'to the satisfying of the soul' — this is wholeness, contentment, and nourishment that goes beyond food to the deepest level. The wicked person, despite perhaps having more material wealth, experiences an inner hunger that is never filled. True satisfaction is a fruit of righteousness. This is an eschatological and daily truth: God satisfies those who walk in His ways.
verses.prayer: God, fill and satisfy my soul today.
verses.discussion_question: What truly satisfies you — not just for a moment but deeply and lastingly?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children distinguish between cravings that are never satisfied (more things, more entertainment, more approval) and the soul-deep satisfaction that comes from God and righteous living?
verses.do_it_today: Think about what truly satisfies your soul — not just your appetite. Spend time in that today: prayer, worship, Scripture, or loving someone well.
verses.illustration_prompt: A contented child sitting peacefully after a satisfying meal, a deep warm glow of soul-satisfaction around them, compared to a figure still reaching and grasping with an empty hollow belly, beautiful close watercolour scene
